title: DCPSC Order No. 22895 (2026-07-02) — The Public Service Commission of the District of Columbia, in Formal Case No. GA2012-11, by Order No. 22895, dated July 2, 2026, granted the request of Viridian
description: The Public Service Commission of the District of Columbia, in Formal Case No. GA2012-11, by Order No. 22895, dated July 2, 2026, granted the request of Viridian Energy PA, LLC (“Applicant”) to surrender its natural gas supplier license. Cancellation of the Applicant’s natural gas supplier license is effective upon the issuance of this Order.

FORMAL CASE NO. GA2012-11, IN THE MATTER OF THE APPLICATION OF 
VIRIDIAN ENERGY PA, LLC TO SURRENDER ITS NATURAL GAS SUPPLIER 
LICENSE IN THE DISTRICT OF COLUMBIA, Order No. 22895 

I. 
INTRODUCTION 
1. 
By this Order,1 the Public Service Commission of the District of Columbia 
(“Commission”) grants the request of Viridian Energy PA, LLC (“Viridian” or “Applicant”) to 
surrender its natural gas supplier license. Cancellation of the Applicant’s natural gas supplier 
license is effective upon the issuance of this Order. 

II. 
BACKGROUND 
2. 
On November 16, 2012, the Commission granted Viridian a license to operate as a 
natural gas supplier in the District of Columbia (“District”) in Order No. 16966.2 On June 5, 2026, 
Viridian filed an Application with the Commission to surrender its natural gas supplier license.3 
Viridian was approved to operate as a marketer of natural gas services, but it conducts no business 
and has no natural gas customers in the District.4 Consequently, Viridian requests to surrender its 
natural gas supplier license.5 

1

authority to act and issue orders on the following matters: . . . m. Applications for the Abandonment of Gas or Electric 
Licenses”). Any party may file a petition for reconsideration of the General Counsel’s decision with the Commission.

III. 
DISCUSSION 

3. 
According to 15 DCMR § 4702.10 (a)(1), a licensed natural gas supplier wishing 
to cease providing services in the District is required to provide written notice to the Commission 
of the licensee’s intention to cease providing natural gas service to its customers and inform its 
customers of the choice to revert to the default service provider or another natural gas supplier. 
Section 4702.10 (a)(2) also requires that the surrendering licensee provide to the Commission an 
example or copy of the notice provided to its customers and, upon the Commission’s receipt of 
such notice, may order the licensee to provide such further notice to its customers or the public as 
the Commission deems necessary, and/or take such other action that the Commission considers 
appropriate.6 

4. 
In the instant case, TES’s Application provides the required notice to the 
Commission of its intention to surrender its natural gas supplier license, effective immediately.7 
Viridian also states that because it provides no natural gas service to customers in the District, the 
notice requirement is inapplicable.8 Accordingly, Viridian’s Application satisfies the notice 
requirement with regard to the cessation of service. 

5. 
In all other respects, Viridian’s Application conforms with Commission 
requirements for a surrendering licensee. The Applicant has provided the case number, order 
number, and the date the Applicant’s license was granted.9 Viridian avers, and Commission 
records confirm, that the Applicant’s most recent survey response indicates no jurisdictional 
revenue and that it owes no outstanding debt or fees.10 In addition, the Applicant attests that it has 
no outstanding consumer complaints.11 Lastly, the Applicant has submitted an affidavit from an 
officer of Viridian attesting to the truth and accuracy of the information submitted.12 

6. 
Based upon the preceding information, the Commission grants Viridian’s request 
to surrender its natural gas supplier license granted by Order No. 16966. Cancellation of Viridian’s 
natural gas supplier license will take effect upon the issuance of this Order. Should Viridian seek 
to re-enter the District’s natural gas market in the future, it shall have to reapply for a natural gas 
supplier license pursuant to Chapter 47 of the Commission’s rules.
